capabilities.name: CAP_CHOWN
capabilities.reason: give each jail's files to the sandbox's own uid and gid

capabilities.name: CAP_SETGID
capabilities.reason: the jailer switches to the sandbox's gid before it execs Firecracker

capabilities.name: CAP_SETUID
capabilities.reason: the jailer switches to the sandbox's uid before it execs Firecracker

capabilities.name: CAP_SYS_ADMIN
capabilities.reason: the jailer's mount namespace, bind mounts and pivot_root

capabilities.name: CAP_MKNOD
capabilities.reason: the jailer creates the device node for /dev/kvm inside the jail

notes: CAP_SYS_CHROOT is absent on purpose: the jailer enters the jail with pivot_root (covered by CAP_SYS_ADMIN), not chroot(2). The real-root step (B-2a-1b) must confirm that; add it back only if that run proves it is used.

CAP_KILL, CAP_FOWNER and CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE are absent on purpose. B-2a-1b is designed to this set: it stops a sandbox by writing cgroup.kill (kernel 5.14 or later), sets a file's mode before it chowns it, and reaps a sandbox-owned tree by fchownat-ing each directory back to root (AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW, which needs only CAP_CHOWN) before it descends.
Writes to cgroup files are ordinary permission checks for root on root-owned cgroupfs files and need no capability.
